paragraphs: Some people think that school should give rewards to students with the best academic results, while others believe that students with improvements should be rewarded. In my opinion, school should reward both high-achieving students and those who show improvements.

On the one hand, students who have the best academic results deserve to be rewarded. First, students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, so they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, propelling towards overall academic gains. Second, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Therefore, students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which can enable them to achieve success in later life.

On the other hand, students who show improvements should be rewarded. Only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, which can cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that both excellent academic results and improvements deserve recognition.
review.overall: Cô thấy em đã triển khai được hai hướng của đề và dùng được một số ý trong dàn ý. Điểm cần ưu tiên là viết câu đủ chủ ngữ và động từ, rồi kiểm tra cấu trúc trước khi dùng câu dài. Bản sửa giữ lập trường thưởng cả hai nhóm và giữ cụm praises and privileges đúng theo dàn ý.

paragraphs: Nowadays, people can use a computer to view historical objects and works of art. For this reason, some people think that public museums and art galleries will no longer be necessary. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought: technology is useful, yet it cannot replace museums and galleries.

Admittedly, technology has made it much easier for people to explore historical and artistic works from home. High-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artifacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. One clear example is Louvre museum, where people can use a virtual museum tour to see famous paintings and historical objects on a computer without travelling to different countries. In addition, these technologies are useful for people who cannot afford travel or have mobility issues, as they can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I believe that public museums and art galleries are necessary. First, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. In fact, seeing these objects directly can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, viewing a historical artefact in person may make its age and authenticity more vivid than an image can. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. They can attract visitors from different places while giving local people an opportunity to learn more about their culture and history. These venues can also foster bonding within the community.
In conclusion, although computers and modern technology allow people to access historical objects, I believe that public museums and art galleries will remain important.

paragraphs: Nowadays, people can use computer to view historical objects and works of art. For this reason, some people think that public museums and art galleries will no longer be necessary. I partly agree with this opinion because technology is useful but it cannot replace museums and galleries.

On the one hand, technology has made it much easier for people to explore historical and artistic works from home. High-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artifacts in remarkable detail, without leaving home. One clear example is louvre museum, where people can use virtual museum tour to see famous paintings and historical objects on a computer, without travelling different countries. In addition, these technologies are useful for people, who cannot afford travel or have mobility issues as they can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

On the other hand, I believe that public museums and art galleries are necessary. First, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. In fact, seeing these objects directly can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, they can attract visitors from different historical places while giving local people an opportunity to learn more about their culture and history. Moreover, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. It magnet for tourism likes a facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, although computers and modern technology allow to access historical objects, I believe that public museums and art galleries will remain important.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people think that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others believe that individuals should be free to take part in any sports or activity. I am personally of the later school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited, because even a minor can cause the death of participant. For example, this may happen when some one is sky diving. However, a ban would be impractical and ineffective, especially remote locations, say mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. Futhermore, it is unrealistic to expect a police officer to follow individuals to prevent them from taking risk. In addition, a prohibition may exist only on paper or even worse, drive practise underground, making it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

Moreover, people should be permitted to do any sports as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. For instance, people who want to try deep ocean diving or bungee Jumping should register with a reputable club, with appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Moreover, beginners should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur. With proper training and necessary precautions, it is safer participation. No activity is entirely risk-free.

In conclusion, banning would be impractical and ineffective. Therefore, people should have freedom to choose any sports or activity, under strict conditions of training and awareness a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: Some people think that children can learn through trial and error, while other people believe that adults should help them avoid mistakes. In my opinion, they should have freedom to make mistakes and be encouraged, provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

On the one hand, opponents of a trial and error approach often emphasise that most mistakes are avoidable. For example, it is unnecessary to get hurt to learn to be careful with knives, fire and electricity. Moreover, it is parents’ responsibility to shield children from harm, forestalling mistakes is a way of fulfilling this duty. In addition, helping children avoid making mistakes gives parents peace of mind because they know that they did their best to protect and raise their child.

Those on the other side, it also has their own valid reasoning. First, parents cannot be around all the time, so preventing them experiment with new things and make mistakes is inevitable. Furthermore, giving children the freedom to make mistakes allow them to learn invaluable lessons that they can learn and these lessons would stand children in good stead in later stages of life. If they are shielded from everything, they may grow up overdependent on others, which is an undesirable trait.

In conclusion, it seems to me that allow children to learn from mistakes, it can prepare for their future, provided that parents have to intervene or give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail their future

Tuy nhiên, việc dựng câu vẫn thiếu kiểm soát ở những chỗ quan trọng: “Those on the other side, it also has” lặp chủ ngữ, “preventing them experiment” sai cấu trúc và “that allow children ..., it can prepare” đứt câu kết. paragraphs: Some people think that children can learn through trial and error, while other people believe that adults should help them avoid mistakes. In my opinion, they should have freedom to make mistakes and be encouraged, provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

On the one hand, opponents of a trial-and-error approach often emphasise that most mistakes are avoidable. For example, it is unnecessary for children to get hurt to learn to be careful with knives, fire and electricity. Moreover, it is parents’ responsibility to shield children from harm. Forestalling mistakes is a way of fulfilling this duty. In addition, helping children avoid making mistakes gives parents peace of mind. This is because they know that they did their best to protect and raise their child.

Those on the other side also have their own valid reasoning. First, parents cannot be around all the time, meaning that children will inevitably experiment with new things and make mistakes. Furthermore, giving children the freedom to make mistakes allows them to learn invaluable lessons that can stand them in good stead in later stages of life. If they are shielded from everything, they may grow up overdependent on others, which is an undesirable trait.

In conclusion, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes can prepare them for the future, provided that parents intervene or give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: The given bar chart illustrates the different kinds of emission sources (oil, coal, gas) of greenhouse gas in the UK from 1990 to 2010.

Overall, There is a decrease in the figures for Coal and Oil, with Coal experiencing the most significant drop. In contrast, Gas increased sharply and became the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions.

To elaborate, In 1990, Gas started at about 230 million tons and then it increased significantly to 320 million tons, became the largest source of emissions. An opposite was observed in Coal, its figure decreased significantly from 310 to 190 million tons at the same time, which made it was the lowest figure on the chart.

Regarding category with less change, Oil decreased from 270 to 210 million tons between 1990 and 2010. However, there was a small increase of about 10 million tons from 1995 to 2000, before it continued to fall.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart compares the amount of carbon emitted from oil, coal and gas in the UK between 1990 and 2010. Figures are measured in millions of tons at five-year intervals.

Overall, emissions from coal and oil declined over the period, with coal showing the larger fall. Gas followed the opposite trend: it rose steadily, overtook the other fuels by 2000 and became the largest source of emissions by the end of the chart.

In 1990, gas emissions were about 220 million tons, the lowest among the three fuels, while coal produced approximately 310 million tons, the highest. The gas figure grew at every recorded point and reached around 320 million tons in 2010. Coal moved in the opposite direction, falling from roughly 310 million tons to 250 million in 2000 and then to about 190 million in 2010. This was the lowest value shown on the chart.

Oil showed less change overall. Its emissions started at about 270 million tons in 1990 and fell to roughly 240 million by 1995. They then recovered by around 20 million tons, reaching about 260 million in 2000, before decreasing again to approximately 210 million in 2010. Across the whole period, oil therefore recorded a net fall of about 60 million tons, compared with coal's decrease of around 120 million tons.

WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Some people believe that history should have a higher priority, while others think that science and technology are more useful in modern world. In my opinion, all of these subjects are equally important.

On the one hand, There is an argument that history more important than other subjects. First, historical lessons can teach students about the lives of their ancestors, which is essential for them to have enough knowledge of the past. In addition, learning from past event can help people understand the meaning of life. For instance, people can learn about wars and conflict and understand that fighting isn't the only solution. Therefore, history can help young people understand their traditions and respect the previous generations.

On the other hand, Science and technology are also important in today's world. In more developed countries, science and technology are already strong and play an important role in education and all the areas of life. For example, people should learn scientific and technological knowledge to do better jobs in the future. Moreover, science and technology can help people solve problems and develop new ideas. However, each subject has an important role, History teach people about the past, science and technology can help people deal with modern life.
In conclusion, history can help people understand the past, science and technology are also useful in today's world. I strongly believe that all of these subjects are equally important

Đoạn lịch sử có ví dụ về chiến tranh và cách giải quyết xung đột, nên ý được minh họa cụ thể hơn. paragraphs.text: Some people believe history deserves a high priority at school, whereas others consider science and technology more useful in the modern world. In my view, these subjects are equally important because they help students understand different kinds of problems.

On the one hand, history can teach students about the lives of earlier generations and the choices that shaped their communities. This knowledge helps young people understand the traditions they have inherited. It can also help them think carefully about conflict. For example, when students study the causes and consequences of a war, they can examine whether negotiation or cooperation might have prevented harm. The point is not that every past conflict has a simple answer, but that historical evidence gives students a way to question the assumption that fighting is the only solution.

On the other hand, science and technology prepare students to investigate and solve current problems. Scientific lessons teach them to test an idea against evidence, while technology classes can show them how to use tools safely and effectively. A student who learns to analyse data or troubleshoot a device, for instance, may be better prepared for technical work later. These abilities also have uses beyond a single job: they can help people judge information about health, energy or the environment. For this reason, science and technology have a valuable place in education alongside history.

In conclusion, history helps students understand the past and the people who shaped it, whereas science and technology equip them to handle many present-day challenges. Since these contributions answer different needs, I believe schools should give both areas serious attention.
